subject: physical-education
title: Unit assessment: giving and receiving feedback about performance, never about bodies under transfer
focus: giving and receiving feedback about performance, never about bodies
essentialQuestion: What makes an activity one that people actually want to come back to?
privacySafeScenario: Redesign a standard activity so that three people with different mobility, experience, and confidence profiles can all participate meaningfully in the same game, and defend each design choice.
studentTask: Learner works giving and receiving feedback about performance, never about bodies inside a real activity with other people present, where the situation arises unplanned and has to be handled in the moment at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, say which feature of giving and receiving feedback about performance, never about bodies degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
completionCriteria: The learner holds giving and receiving feedback about performance, never about bodies inside a real activity with other people present, where the situation arises unplanned and has to be handled in the moment, in whatever version their body and setting allow.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.
adaptationChoices: The redesign may be written, diagrammed, described aloud, or trialed practically. Practical trial is optional.
extensionChallenge: Design the next progression of giving and receiving feedback about performance, never about bodies yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
The redesign may be written, diagrammed, described aloud, or trialed practically. Practical trial is optional.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice where giving and receiving feedback about performance, never about bodies shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
